text: Write a program where overriding and overloading disagree in a single line. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: static class A { String who() { return "A"; } }
explanation: Verified: `B` then `A-overload`. One object, two resolution rules. The override is dispatched at run time from what the object *is*; the overload was chosen at compile time from what the variable was *declared* as. That is the whole contrast, and it is why Chapter 12 advises against overloading methods that do different things — the reader cannot see which one runs.
